newsitem.title: USA: Oregon Treasurer warns measure could harm ratings.
newsitem.headline: Oregon Treasurer warns measure could harm ratings.

text.p: Oregon state Treasurer Jim Hill warned on Tuesday that the state's credit ratings could come under pressure if a controversial ballot measure passes in November.
On Monday, Standard & Poor's Corp raised its rating to AA from AA-minus on Oregon's $3.7 billion of general obligation bonds. Hill said the move would save taxpayers tens of millions of dollars.
"However, our celebration may be short lived if 47 passes," Hill said, referring to ballot initiative 47.
Measure 47 calls for an amendment to the state Constitution that would prohibit bonded indebtedness for certain capital construction and improvements.

Should the measure pass on the November ballot, the state would almost certainly face increased pressure from local governments to ease the burden of property tax losses, S&P warned in a statement on Monday.
Hill said in a statement that the state's bond ratings could come under pressure if measure 47 passes.
"I am very concerned with the potential impacts that measure 47 may have on the state's good news," Hill said.
If the measure passes, Hill said S&P would be forced to reevaluate the state's bond ratings.
